description: The Anthology Engine, the per-client orchestrator that turns ONE participant's universal Convert and Flow form submission into ONE gated, quality-controlled 2,000 to 3,500 word anthology chapter (never twelve), delivered as BOTH a Google Doc and a designed PDF with no font below 14 point, links pushed to standardized Convert and Flow contact custom fields keyed by contact_id. It owns ALL external input and output and CALLS Skill 54 (Anthology Writer) as its authoring core; it never re-authors the chapter pipeline. Four layers: a deterministic intake router; an Airtable-backed durable multi-participant ledger (contact_id plus anthology_id); the Skill 54 authoring core extended with the Skill 52 avatar handoff and the newly pinned prompts; Google Drive plus PDF plus Convert and Flow delivery; and the producer and participant surfaces INSIDE the client's own Command Center (a seeded Anthology department board, home-screen tiles, and a token-scoped participant page). Every stage is an idempotent, resumable job against the ledger; a crash, a credit outage, or a six-month pause costs nothing. Runs S0 intake to S9 anthology assembly through one sanctioned entry (anthology-engine-entry.sh). The producer is the OpenClaw box owner; participants are external co-authors with no login. Runtime uses the client's own configured provider chain only. Move in silence: operator-verbose, client-silent, only three sanctioned nudge templates ever reach a client. Sibling of Skill 53 (Book Writer) and Skill 54 (Anthology Writer); it deprecates neither. Trigger with "run the anthology engine", "start an anthology", "onboard an anthology producer", "assemble the anthology", or an inbound anthology intake webhook.
